source.title: What's going on with Per-Component Weight Updates?

record.tranche_reason: The post tests whether component-wise gradient or weight-change magnitudes provide a useful signal around a known induction-head phase change, using a different measurement from the original grokking studies.
record.gate_note: The induction-head analysis reports weight differences between consecutive checkpoints as a proxy for gradient changes and relates them to the phase change. The ResNet section reports gradient-norm patterns, but does not identify or measure a grokking event or test accuracy there, so those patterns are not recorded as rows. No training-accuracy/test-accuracy trajectory or removal of memorizing components is reported.
record.test_reason: The post does not test any version. Its measure is the L2 norm of weight changes between consecutive checkpoints, a proxy for gradient size. It applies this to the induction-head phase change in pre-existing attention-only LMs, which is not a train/test grokking delay on algorithmic data. It does not trace circuit formation or the removal of memorizing components. It does not test whether a mechanism-based progress measure anticipates a test-accuracy jump. The ResNet run has no delayed-generalization event. The question it asks, whether naive weight-change norms flag a phase change, is a related but different construct, so it is recorded under fits_no_version.
record.authors_conclusion: Mostly correct. The author concludes that naive L2 norms of weight changes give no clear grokking signal. They still find the drop in gradient norm near the phase change striking and speculate that it is a double-descent-like effect. More work, a dataset of known groks, and self-trained models are needed.
record.recipe_differences: This is an exploratory measurement study, not a reproduction of the original algorithmic-task training setup. It uses pre-existing induction-head checkpoints and measures checkpoint weight differences as a proxy, alongside a separate ResNet gradient-norm exploration.
record.method_sensitivity: The induction-head signal is affected by model depth and head selection; the author also notes later variation, probably from learning-rate scheduling changes near 5B tokens.

fits_no_version.finding: In 1L/2L/3L attention-only models, global and per-head weight-change norms shift around the induction-head phase change. The shift also appears in the 1L model, which lacks induction heads. Later variation, likely from learning-rate schedule changes near 5B tokens, dwarfs it, and induction heads do not consistently stand out.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Naive per-component weight-update norms do not provide a specific signal of phase changes or grokking.

fits_no_version.finding: On ResNet/CIFAR-10, per-layer gradient norms show a double-descent-like shape, with batch-norm and downsample gradients rising after an initial drop. No generalization event is linked to these patterns.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Per-layer gradient-norm dynamics in standard vision training show non-monotonic patterns not tied to delayed generalization.

record.problems: Small exploratory study; it uses pre-existing induction-head checkpoints rather than training the models itself. Weight differences between checkpoints are only a proxy for gradients. Results are chiefly qualitative and plot-based, with no uncertainty estimates or quantitative analysis of predictive performance. The ResNet results do not include a measured grokking event or test-accuracy trajectory.
record.rows_left_out: The ResNet gradient-norm observations are not included as rows because the post does not connect them to a measured grokking or delayed-generalization event. The post also notes that the induction-head models' global and per-head plots are shown, but does not report numerical values in the text.

untested.parts: No algorithmic task and no train/test accuracy curves.
No circuit-formation tracing, no memorization-removal measure, and no test of whether a progress measure anticipates a test-accuracy jump.
The ResNet/CIFAR-10 run shows no delayed generalization, and initialization scale and weight norm are not varied.
The induction-head models are small attention-only LMs, and no delayed generalization is measured in them.
Learned algorithms are not compared across runs.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests/T2' guess and its V2 limits_scope label are removed. The induction-head phase change is not the grokking delay that V2 describes. A weight-change norm is not a mechanistic progress measure, and the post gives no quantitative anticipation analysis. The post is an exploratory, qualitative, plot-based blog post with no uncertainty estimates.

versions.untested_parts: No small algorithmic dataset training-accuracy/test-accuracy trajectory or delay-versus-training-set-size comparison.

The post tests whether gradient/weight-change magnitude signals a phase change, but does not trace gradual formation of a generalizing circuit, measure removal of memorizing components, or test whether a continuous measure anticipates a test-accuracy jump.
The ResNet experiment does not report grokking-like delayed generalization or vary initialization scale or weight norm.
No realistic large-model pretraining or fine-tuning experiment is reported.
No efficiency account, critical dataset size, weight-decay intervention, or ungrokking test.
The post does not identify or compare algorithms learned across runs.
No adaptive-optimizer instability or floating-point softmax artifact is controlled or tested.

rows.operation_detail: Measured squared weight differences between consecutive checkpoints, averaged by parameter count, as a proxy for gradient magnitude; global norm.
rows.measure: Global weight-change magnitude (reported as a proxy for gradient magnitude)
rows.value: A large change in the direction of gradient magnitude occurs around the phase change; the change also occurs in 1L and later variation dwarfs it.
rows.locator: Induction Heads; Discussion; global weight-change plots
rows.note: The prose says the pattern occurs in 1L as well, although the induction heads of interest are in the 2L and 3L models.
rows.check: The 1L model has no induction heads, so it is effectively the control. Its weight-change shift near the phase window shows the signal is not specific. A weight-change norm cannot show V2's gradual circuit formation or memorization cleanup.

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The weight-change signal is ambiguous: a phase-related shift is also seen in 1L, it can fail to clearly distinguish induction heads from other heads, and later variation dwarfs it (r1-r6).
